clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old Indian female presented to cardiology with uncontrolled hypertension, exertional angina class 2, malaise, and fatigue. Clinical examination revealed asymmetric blood pressure (150/77 mmHg left arm vs 179/95 mmHg right arm) and asymmetric radial pulses (weak and thready left radial artery vs full and bounding right radial artery). Laboratory workup showed elevated inflammatory markers (elevated CRP and ESR) with normal white blood cell count. MR angiography revealed complete thrombosis of the left subclavian and left common carotid arteries with 80-90% luminal narrowing of the long segmental lower thoracic and abdominal aorta. Peripheral angiography confirmed multiple stenoses in the right subclavian artery, approximately 80% stenosis in bilateral renal arteries, and non-visualization of the left subclavian artery. The patient subsequently underwent percutaneous angioplasty with drug-eluting stents in the LAD and LCX coronaries and was placed on dual antiplatelet therapy.
